We aim to maximize
\[
M = \sum^8_{i=1} \sum^7_{j=1} \left( |a_{i,j+1} - a_{i,j}| + |a_{j+1,i} - a_{j,i}| \right),
\]
which sums the absolute differences between all horizontally and vertically adjacent cells in an \(8 \times 8\) grid containing the integers \(1\) through \(64\) exactly once. The grid graph is bipartite with two color classes of equal size and degree sums. To maximize \(M\), we place the 32 largest numbers (\(33\)–\(64\)) on one color class and the 32 smallest numbers (\(1\)–\(32\)) on the other, ensuring every edge connects a larger number to a smaller number. Within each class, we assign numbers to maximize the weighted difference
\[
M = \sum_{\text{large}} \deg(v) \cdot a_v - \sum_{\text{small}} \deg(v) \cdot a_v.
\]
For the large set (say black cells), we assign the largest numbers to cells with the highest degree: interior cells (degree 4) get \(47\)–\(64\), edge cells (degree 3) get \(35\)–\(46\), and corners (degree 2) get \(33\)–\(34\). For the small set (white cells), to minimize the weighted sum, we assign the smallest numbers to the highest degree cells: interior cells get \(1\)–\(18\), edge cells get \(19\)–\(30\), and corners get \(31\)–\(32\).

Computing the weighted sums:
\[
\begin{aligned}
S_{\text{black}} &= 2(33 + 34) + 3(35 + \cdots + 46) + 4(47 + \cdots + 64) \\
&= 2 \cdot 67 + 3 \cdot 486 + 4 \cdot 999 = 134 + 1458 + 3996 = 5588, \\
S_{\text{white}} &= 2(31 + 32) + 3(19 + \cdots + 30) + 4(1 + \cdots + 18) \\
&= 2 \cdot 63 + 3 \cdot 294 + 4 \cdot 171 = 126 + 882 + 684 = 1692.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(M = 5588 - 1692 = 3896\). The remainder when \(3896\) is divided by \(1000\) is \(896\).

\boxed{896}
